features.name: Town decrees (curfew, entry controls, garbage collection, social housing, strict law, begging ban)
features.summary: Each town or fort can carry up to six standing decrees. The player issues or revokes them for gold from the fief-management screen, and AI lords issue and revoke them on their own. Every decree trades prosperity, crime, disease or the townsfolk's goodwill against each other.
features.mechanics: Each decree is a 0/1 flag in party slots 264-269 (curfew, entry controls, garbage collection, social housing, strict law enforcement, begging ban). Names and descriptions come from get_decree_details. The player toggles a decree in prsnt:center_management/t4, which shows a gold-cost confirmation. AI lords decide in troop_does_business_in_center via decide_decree_enact and decide_decree_revoke. Those two scripts roll against the lord's attribute, the town's prosperity (party slot 46), the lord's personality (troop slot 52) and a culture bonus for 'barbarian' factions. Effects read the flags in these places: cf_center_night_bandits_check (strig:188/189) for night bandit infestation, which curfew, housing and strict law affect; strig:158 for the epidemic chance, which garbage collection lowers; strig:157 for monthly-ish relation changes (housing raises relation, entry controls and strict law lower it); get_center_ideal_prosperity (housing, strict law, begging ban); do_merchant_town_trade and menu:control at the town gate (entry controls); town menu options and rumours (curfew); and center_get_capital. A notification fires when an AI lord enacts or revokes a decree.

features.name: Settlement events and epidemics (inherits ad457.settlement_disasters_epidemics; acan adds harvests, winters, sanitation and wider effects)
features.summary: Towns and villages get one active local event at a time: a good or poor harvest, a harsh or mild winter, drought, insects, an earthquake, a fire, or a disease outbreak (consumption, fevers, plague, measles and others). For its duration the event changes prosperity growth, rents, recruits and town-dweller talk. When the player owns the place they are notified, and for an epidemic they can order a quarantine.
features.mechanics: Party slot 324 holds the active event id. get_event_details turns the id into a name, a description, a prosperity-rate percentage (reg0) and a prosperity delta (reg1); its id bands encode event type and severity. strig:158 (about hourly) picks a random town, rolls an epidemic weighted by month (winter is worse) and by sanitation (garbage-collection decree party 266, sewers improvement party 294, hospital improvement party 287), picks a disease, applies change_center_prosperity, sets slot 324 and notifies the holder with menu_epidemic_outbreak (option: 'Order a quarantine'). strig:163 rolls earthquakes in seismic regions (cf_can_have_earthquake reads the region in party 68) and sends menu_disaster_event. calculate_weekly_rents ages and clears events. Readers: get_center_ideal_prosperity, calculate_weekly_rents, calculate_latifundium_rents, get_volunteer_limits (fewer recruits), process_player_enterprise, get_rumor_to_s61, town and village menus and dweller dialogs.
evidence: dis acan get_event_details: id bands -> poor/good harvest, conquered, harsh/mild winter, earthquake, fire, drought, insects, Rome fire, consumption, slow fever, camp fever, plague, measles
dis acan strig:158: month weighting, slot 266/294/287 modifiers, sets party 324, add_notification_menu menu_epidemic_outbreak

features.name: Faction treasuries with a weekly budget: income/spending categories, corruption, tax fraud, embezzlement trials
features.summary: Every kingdom keeps a real treasury that is refilled and drained weekly by categorised income (taxes, edict taxes, tributes) and spending (army upkeep, cohort refills, salaries, subsidies). Corruption skims a share of income. A ruler-player can read an imperial budget report, pay into or take from the treasury, and risk an embezzlement trial if they take too much.
features.mechanics: add_to_faction_bugdet(category_slot, faction, amount) (62 callers) adds an amount to a category slot on the faction. Weekly netting (below) shows faction slots 270-274 are the income buckets and 262-269 the spending buckets. When the player is the ruler, positive postings to 270/271/273 are boosted, and negative postings to 266/267 shrunk, by household quality (get_household_modifier). trig:5 (weekly) runs weekly_imperial_balance, which sums and clears 262-269 (spending) and 270-274 (income). It handles slot 275 (the ruler's pay or draw, sign convention not resolved): it pays the ruler via add_to_troop_wealth, or event_player_takes_money_imperial_treasury when the ruler is the player, and adds it to the income side. It adds a corruption share of income (calculate_imperial_corruption: a percentage that a census ($conducted_census), extra tax collectors ($control_tax) and minister/chamberlain household quality reduce) plus 4% of faction slot 43 to the spending side, and books net = income + slot 275 - spending through add_to_faction_treasury (faction slots 43/44). calculate_bureaucratic_costs and calculate_edict_tax are posted from calculate_weekly_rents (strig:53/196). prsnt:imperial_budget_report and prsnt:budget_report draw the report (generate_imperial_bugdet_report, 427 stmts). The player-ruler can pay into or withdraw from the treasury (dlg:4620 imperial_treasury_action_take_money). Taking money raises suspicion, which leads to menu:caught_embezzle_punished and trial dialogs (trial_guilty -> remove_office_from_troop). calculate_staff_salary itemises minister, praefectus urbani and tax-collector salaries.
evidence: dis acan weekly_imperial_balance: sums/clears faction 262-269 (:l1, spending side) and 270-274 (:l4, income side); corruption % of :l4 added to :l1; :l4 += slot 275; :l4 -= :l1; add_to_faction_treasury(:l4)

explain acan add_to_faction_treasury: '{reg0} denarii have been added to/taken from the imperial treasury'
text 'Edict': str_faction_taxes_edicts / str_faction_spending_edicts budget lines
dis acan add_to_faction_bugdet: faction_set_slot(category) += amount; household bonus on positive 270/271/273 and on negative 266/267 when the player rules

features.name: Influence points, Senate support and kingdom-wide edicts voted in the Senate
features.summary: Influence becomes a currency the player spends on political actions: asking for titles, forcing peace talks, bribing lords and changing governors. The ruler also needs the Senate's support (40 senators, won by persuasion or bribes), and support passes or blocks kingdom edicts. Edicts are laws that add taxes or subsidies to the budget and raise or lower unrest.
features.mechanics: Influence is stored in troop slot 6 and changed by change_influence (31 callers, 475 reachable entry points: dialogs, menus, quests). get_influence_cost_for_decision prices a decision from a base cost adjusted by culture difference, piety ($player_piety), the target lord's personality, honour, rank and province modifiers; it is used by the peace-declaration, bribe, honorary-title and governor-change dialogs and presentations. Senate support is a percentage on trp_senator_dummy slot 19, scaled to 40 senators. change_senate_support adjusts it, lowers the player's controversy (troop slot 166) and, per point, may raise relation with Rome (persuasion) or cost honour (bribery). prsnt:senate runs cf_menu_condition_senate (274 stmts, 93-block closure), the hub for speeches (give_a_speech), Senate decisions and office removal. Edicts are globals $edict1..$edict11 (for example libelli, securitatis publica, Christiani, slave manumission tax). Each is proposed in menu:debate_in_senat_2, where a majority vote passes or fails it, or issued through minister dialogs (dlg:4159-4178 edicts2). They feed calculate_bureaucratic_costs and calculate_edict_tax (budget), strig:19 (unrest/stability), strig:176, calculate_latifundium_rents and display_policy_string_to_reg.
evidence: dis acan change_influence: troop slot 6, messages 'Your influence has changed from {reg11} to {reg12}'

features.name: Ranks, offices and honorary titles (legate, auxiliary prefect, governor, Quaestor..Censor) with triumphs
features.summary: Lords and the player hold formal offices: command of a standing legion, command of an auxiliary unit, a provincial governorship, and honorary titles (Quaestor, Aedile, Consul, Censor) handed out by the ruler. Office decides party size, banner and title. Losing a trial, resigning or angering the ruler strips it. Victories earn triumph points and a public triumph.
features.mechanics: troop_set_rank (103 callers) writes the rank slot: troop slot 178 = legion commanded (also mirrored in trp_province_array slot 215+n), slot 179 = auxiliary unit template commanded (mirrored at 250+n). It then updates $g_rank for the player, re-forms the lord's party (party_update_cohorts), and resets the title, the banner and every owned fief's banner icon. remove_office_from_troop (trial verdicts, resignation, leaving the faction) clears offices and calls find_new_commander_for_legion / _for_aux / faction_dismisses_marshall. Honorary titles are handed out by ai_assign_title (relation/renown driven; give_honorary_titles at game start; menu_honorary_title_granted) and can be usurped (usurp_honor_title_with_help) or lost when the holder angers others (destroy_center text). Provinces are imperial or senatorial (prsnt:make_province_imperial / make_province_senatorial, governor_selection, governor_change). get_province_relation_modifier rates provinces as unruly or easy to rule. troop_change_triumph_points accumulates triumph points, and troop_holds_triumph / triumph_marsh_start stage the triumph mission (mst_triumph). change_lord_party_to_fit_rank sizes the party to the office.

features.name: Unit-based army organisation: standing legions with HQs, cohort-limited party size, unit recruitment and province manpower
features.summary: Armies are built and refilled in whole units ('cohorts': officers, nobles, recruits and mercenaries) instead of single soldiers. How many units a party may hold depends on rank, offices, fiefs and culture. Standing legions exist as permanent parties with a headquarters town and a commander, are refilled from the province's manpower pool and paid from the faction budget. When their HQ falls they relocate.
features.mechanics: get_cohort_limit (13 callers) returns the unit cap: towns 381/406, castles 401 (garrison capacity codes); the player 10-25 by $g_rank and emperor status; a legion legate (troop 178) 16-17; an auxiliary prefect (179) 11-12; otherwise 4 plus culture, faction-strength (faction 225), marshal and fiefs bonuses, capped at 25. prsnt:recruit_cohorts / manage_cohorts / manage_cohorts_town let the player hire, refill, dismiss or donate whole units, with building-culture requirements (cf_can_hire_cohort -> get_building_culture) and cost/upkeep lines. cohort_describe_strength_to_s5_and_refil runs periodically (strig:28/58/64/121) for AI and player parties: it counts each unit, buys replacements (game_get_join_cost) from the faction budget (add_to_faction_bugdet) or the lord's wealth, and takes men from the province pools (take_recruits_from_province: party slots 83/84/152). party_update_cohorts writes the unit roster into party slots 10-24 of a lord's party. strig:192 (daily) hires for legions, finds new commanders (find_new_commander_for_legion/aux) and moves a captured HQ (find_new_headquarter_for_legion -> get_closest_walled_center_of_faction, legion_hq_set_banner). Garrisons are kept in units too (cohort_refil_garrison after a capture, update_center_garrison).

features.name: Private estates (latifundia) on the map with production buildings, slave labour and weekly rents
features.summary: The player can acquire land next to a village; it appears on the campaign map as their estate. There they build production works (vineyard and winepress, olive grove and oil press, silk and velvet, and more), assign slaves as labour, and draw weekly rent. Fires and other events can damage it, and how slaves are treated matters.
features.mechanics: A village-elder dialog (dlg:8881 barb_estate_talk_3 / dlg:8904 lad_talk3) calls spawn_latifundium, which spawns a map party ('Latifundia/Estate near {s0}') via spawn_party and stores its buildings in party slots 214-243. get_building_details_lat gives each building's name, cost, build time and product. Weekly calculate_weekly_rents (strig:53 / strig:196) calls calculate_latifundium_rents (210 stmts): output per building x labour (get_labour_slave_skill_modifier on the slave troops present), times the event modifier (get_event_details, e.g. fire), honour (get_honor_factor) and household quality (get_household_modifier), with slave treatment/manumission settings ($g_slave_treatment, $g_slave_manu, edict11 slave tax). menu:latifundium and prsnt:estate_report show state, and menu_event_latifundium_fire_damage / _nodamage report fires. A blacksmith on the estate can improve items (dlg:11325 lat_item_improve).
evidence: explain acan spawn_latifundium: texts 'Latifundia near {s0}', 'Estate near {s0}', building list
explain acan calculate_latifundium_rents: callees get_labour_slave_skill_modifier/get_event_details/get_honor_factor/get_household_modifier

features.name: Culture-specific fief buildings with culture drift (inherits ad457.center_buildings_management; acan adds culture shift and piety effects)
features.summary: Towns and forts have about 34 building types, each with a name, description and cost that depend on the settlement's culture (a Roman sewer becomes a Persian kariz or a British sacred grove). AI lords build too. Finished buildings raise prosperity, health and relations, unlock unit recruitment and can gradually shift the settlement's culture.
features.mechanics: get_improvement_details (828 vs Native 32 stmts) dispatches on the improvement slot (party 271-304) and the settlement culture to return name, description and cost (e.g. 294 sewers: rome/eastern/germanic/british/dacian/nomadic variants; 287 hospital; 291 training; 293 barracks). The player orders buildings from prsnt:center_management, and AI lords via improve_center from troop_does_business_in_center. strig:82 (about every 2 min) runs cf_check_building_finished (235 stmts): it completes the work, applies prosperity, renown, honour and relation changes and add_piety_culture_effect, and can call change_culture_of_center, which moves a settlement to the builder's culture (walkers, town watch, icon). Buildings then gate unit recruitment (cf_can_hire_cohort -> get_building_culture) and feed the epidemic roll (287/294).

features.name: Household staff: captured prisoners made cooks and household slaves, with quality affecting feasts, budget and estates
features.summary: A captured prisoner can be assigned as a household cook or household slave. The number of slots grows with renown. Staff quality becomes a 'household modifier' read by feasts, lord conversations, estate rents and imperial corruption.
features.mechanics: dlg:9497 prisoner_chat_add_household_slave and prsnt:select_household_slave / household_management call assign_household_slave / assign_household_cook. These copy the prisoner into a household troop (trp_household_slave_1..trp_household_end, trp_household_cook_1), generate a face between keys, name it by culture and copy its inventory, writing troop slot 10. get_cook_limit / get_slave_limit and the renown thresholds cap the count; describe_cook_quality_to_s1 and describe_slave_skills_to_s0 describe them. get_household_modifier (23 callers) turns staff skills into a percentage used by add_to_faction_bugdet, calculate_imperial_corruption, calculate_latifundium_rents, feast and lord-talk conditions.

features.name: Slave economy: prisoners and conquered populations become culture-specific slaves, sold by town slave traders, slavers and special dealers
features.summary: Captured soldiers and the population of a sacked town are converted into slaves of their culture. Town slave traders, bandit slavers and special dealers buy and sell them. Slaves are then used as estate labour, household staff or for profit, and an edict can tax manumission.
features.mechanics: troop_to_slave_mapping (326 stmts) maps any troop to its culture's slave troop (male or female) and is called when prisoners are added (party_prisoners_add_party_prisoners/companions, both modified Native) and from menu:castle_taken_plunder / menu:exterminate_population / strig:92. trig:17 refills slave merchants (refill_slave_merchant -> refill_slave_trader_town / _bandit / _special, troop slots 102-130 as stock), and mst_slave_market / slave_hideout are the visit scenes. count_party_slaves, remove_slaves_from_party, apply_changes_to_slave_trader, get_slave_merchant_troop and menu:camp_make_slaves handle party-side actions. $edict11 (Vicesima libertatis) taxes manumissions in the budget.

features.name: Patron deity, piety and sacrifices, with divine boons and in-battle miracles
features.summary: The player chooses a patron god and builds piety by sacrificing at temples and priests and by pious acts. A sacrifice rolls for a boon (protection in fight, leadership, favour, wisdom, experience). In battle, a favoured player may get a miracle every few seconds: extra strength, courage for nearby troops, or healing. Piety also changes the price of political actions and how lords see you.
features.mechanics: Piety is the global $player_piety, changed by add_piety (62 callers: dialogs, menus, strigs) and rated by get_piety_impact ('Hated by the gods'..'Honored by the gods'). Worship dialogs (dlg:10413/10494 worship_gods) set the patron (troop slot 23), and deity_compatibility_with_culture and add_piety_culture_effect adjust relations by the god's fit with a culture. make_sacrifice (priest dialogs dlg:10425/10465/10502) costs gold, rolls 'Probability {reg10} / Dice {reg11}' and grants a timed boon (quest 27 slot as the boon store, $can_sacrific cooldown). perform_miracle runs every 3 s in about 29 battle templates (gated by cf_can_perform_miracle) and can boost the player's strength, raise troop courage (agent slot 3) or heal. visit_temple and the temple submenus give scenes for each god. player_change_religion changes faith. Piety feeds get_influence_cost_for_decision and the conspiracy check.

features.name: Player health and mortality: sickness accumulates, can be treated, and can kill the character
features.summary: The player has a hidden ill-health score. It rises from wounds, drinking, orgies, disease and hardship, and falls with baths, barbers, herbal remedies and rest at a villa. Each day a very unhealthy character risks a 'Death waits' event; resisting it worsens health, and accepting it ends the game.

(+25 sickness, back to the map) or 'Take her hand' (menu_death, game over).

features.name: Permanent field camps commanded by a companion, which store troops and loot, ransom your prisoners and attract bandits
features.summary: Near a friendly town the player can found a permanent camp (paid in gold) and leave a companion in charge. The camp holds troops, prisoners and goods. Every few hours the commander sells the prisoners for you, and the more valuables are stored, the more bandits it attracts, so it can come under attack.
features.mechanics: menu:create_pcamp checks gold, an available companion, a leadership-based camp limit and distance to the nearest centre (get_closest_center_and_minor), then calls set_player_camp_commander (party slots 25/26, troop slots 10/28 on the commander; name '{s0}'s Camp'). menu:player_camp is the camp's own menu. strig:29 (every 6 h) runs pcamp_ransom_prisoners: it sells prisoners at game_get_prisoner_price and calls calc_player_camp_bandit_attraction (stored inventory value -> troop slots 32/33), which drives bandit raids defended in mst_camp_defend (with camp_defenders_move_to_defender_position). Dialogs let you replace the commander (replace_player_camp_commander) or disband the camp (disband_player_camp, cleanup_player_camp_slot); find_closest_player_camp and get_player_camp_scene support travel and scenes.

features.name: Enlisting as a common soldier: career progress gated by about 30 random service events
features.summary: The player can enlist in a lord's army as a soldier. They receive the unit's kit and advance through service, but promotion needs points earned from about 30 event menus (drinking, marsh duty, training, temptations, punishments) and drill sessions. Leaving or being discharged returns the player's own gear.

It sets $enlisted_party, starts the service quest, and freelancer_add_player_items / freelancer_equip_troop swap the player's gear for the assigned troop's ('The equipment of a {s21}: {s2} is assigned to you'). features.name: Conspiracies against the ruler (palace assassination fights) and treason or embezzlement trials
features.summary: A player-ruler who enters their palace or castle can be ambushed by conspirators. The odds depend on unrest, honour, piety, right to rule, edicts and how much the lords hate them, and an attack becomes a fight in the palace. Lords, and the player, can also be put on trial for treason or embezzlement; friends and paid agents can intervene, and a guilty verdict strips offices.
features.mechanics: menu:town options town_castle / visit_palace call cf_conspiracy_check (137 stmts). It scores lords' relations (troop_get_relation_with_troop), $g_unrest, $player_honor, $player_piety, $player_right_to_rule and $edict6, respects a cooldown ($g_last_assassination_attempt_time), and on success jumps to menu_conspiracy, whose 'continue' fills the palace scene with the conspirators from trp_array_villa_feast and starts mst_conspiracy_fight. Trials: indict_lord_for_treason (modified Native), menu:trial_guilty and dlg trial_guilty (remove_office_from_troop, gold fines). Wives/ladies or bought agents (Locusta, Crispinilla) can intervene via intervene_treason (troop slot 22, quest 6). Embezzlement from the treasury leads to menu_caught_embezzle_punished.

features.name: Civil wars, usurping the throne, annexing the losing side, and defeated kingdoms reborn
features.summary: A realm can split into civil war, after which the winner annexes the losers' lords and fiefs. A strong player or lord can usurp the throne, which reshuffles factions, ranks, titles, fiefs and marriages. Every two days the game checks whether a destroyed kingdom can be restored with a new lord.
features.mechanics: activate_main_story_civil_war / start_year_of_four set $g_civil_war and split factions (story-driven in acan). usurp_faction (177 stmts) moves lords between factions (change_troop_faction), adjusts relations, kills or divorces where needed (kill_lord_lady, troop_divorce_troop), re-ranks (troop_set_rank), regrants fiefs (give_center_to_lord2), resets titles, banners and party sizes, and assigns honorary titles. cf_annex_faction (from dlg:6222 end_civil_war_captured_enemies or menu notification_civil_war_faction_defeated) folds the defeated side's lords and centres into the victor and changes right to rule. strig:87 (every 48 h) checks for defeated factions and calls reactivate_kingdom, which can spawn a new lord (give_birth_to_lord), return exiles (dplmc_lord_return_from_exile) and hand back a centre, then sends menu_notification_kingdom_restored / _liberated. become_emperor finalises a usurpation for the player.
evidence: explain acan usurp_faction: 13 callees incl. change_troop_faction/kill_lord_lady/troop_set_rank/give_center_to_lord2/ai_assign_title
explain acan cf_annex_faction: callers end_civil_war dialog + civil-war-defeated menu

features.name: Conquest aftermath: keep or plunder, exterminate/enslave the population, raze the settlement, repopulate and shift its culture
features.summary: After taking a town or fort the player chooses its fate: keep it, plunder it, kill or enslave the population, or raze it entirely. Exterminated settlements can be repopulated with the conqueror's people, which changes the place's culture (walkers, town watch, recruits, map icon). Harsh choices anger lords and can cost honorary titles.
features.mechanics: menu:castle_taken_plunder / castle_taken_keepplunder / castle_taken_native / desert_town_loot2 handle plunder. menu:exterminate_population (152 stmts) turns locals into prisoners/slaves (troop_to_slave_mapping, party_add_wounded_members_as_prisoners), recomputes production and consumption, and may call destroy_center (prosperity crash, party destroyed, quests aborted, faction strength recalculated; text '{s21} is angry about {s20} and he may lose his honorary title!'). menu:repopulate ('Kill them all' special-tax option) and cf_check_building_finished call change_culture_of_center, which rewrites the settlement's culture, walkers (center_set_walker_to_type), town watch troops (update_town_watch: party 381-384) and walled icon (set_icon_for_walled_center), with the notice '{s0} changed from {s2} to {s1} culture'. Volunteers then follow the new culture via get_unit_according_to_subculture and get_peasant_warrior_for_culture.
evidence: explain acan menu:exterminate_population: callees troop_to_slave_mapping, get_unit_according_to_subculture, mst_center_plunder
explain acan destroy_center: callers castle_taken_plunder / desert_town_loot2 / exterminate_population, faction_recalculate_strength

features.name: Ports, landings and ferries as map parties, sea trade routes, embarking armies and an overseas merchant fleet
features.summary: At game start every coastal town gets a port party on the water, plus landings and ferries, so armies can embark from a port (minimum crew 15) and sail. Sea trade routes link coastal towns, and AI parties use sea lanes. Through a dialog the player can also send a merchant fleet to India for profit.
features.mechanics: add_ports_jetty_and_ferry_system (game_start) spawns 'Port of {s1}' / 'Landing near {s2}' parties at get_next_water_position near each coastal centre ($g_number_ports; party slots 39/40/41 link port and centre). initialize_sea_trade_routes / set_sea_trade_route_between_centers build up to 15 routes per town, and cf_select_most_profitable_coastal_town_at_peace_with_faction_in_trade_route picks targets. menu:town_port 'Set sail from port' and menu:landet_ships_encounter call switch_to_water_consequences / switch_to_land_consequences (party icon, $players_ship, warn about leaving caravans behind). game_get_party_speed_multiplier (210 stmts) handles land/water moves with $wind_power. map_sea_ai_1-3 (strig:90 daily and others) send AI parties by sea (get_closest_port via party_set_ai_state), and bandits_go_to_lairs moves pirates/bandits. calculate_sea_caravan_cost prices the India fleet (dlg:10215).

features.name: Thrust-only ('noswing') weapon swap for infantry in tight formation (spear and pike wall)
features.summary: When infantry form a close formation, every long enough thrusting weapon is swapped for a thrust-only twin, so men in the ranks stab past their comrades instead of swinging into them. On formation end or death the real weapon is swapped back, so loot stays correct.
features.mechanics: init_noswing_weapons (ti_before_mission_start in 10 battle templates, 278 stmts) writes a two-way map in item slot 46: weapon <-> its 'noswing_' twin (139 noswing item entries in item_kinds1.txt, which sit past itm_items_end). form_infantry calls switch_to_noswing_weapons(agent, min_length) for each formation member: it loops weapon slots 0-3, and for a thrusting weapon (cf_is_thrusting_weapon) at least min_length long swaps to the slot-46 twin. switch_from_noswing_weapons restores the original from formation_end and on ti_on_agent_killed_or_wounded in the same 10 templates.

features.name: Inherited VC battle stack: battlegroup formations AI, war cries/horns/shield taunts, courage spreading, shield bash; plus a ratio-based rout rule
features.summary: acan's battle layer is Viking Conquest's: battlegroup formations with field tactics for the AI, horse-archer skirmishing, war cries, horns and shield taunts that lift courage, morale spreading from nearby deaths, and an AI shield bash. Its own additions are a rout rule (a side can only rout once its losses pass a set share of the men still standing), bodyguards in town scenes and a death camera.
features.mechanics: Formations: store_battlegroup_data, form_infantry/archers/cavalry, team_field_melee_tactics, team_field_ranged_tactics, player_order_formations and battlegroup_* are 97-100% opcode-identical to VC (compare). Immersion: agent_perform_warcry/horn, shield_taunt_trigger, change_courage_around_agent (82% vs VC) and shield_bash_trigger (85% vs VC) run in about 29-44 templates. acan/ad457 add cf_calculate_battle_ratio (every 10 s, j_num_* globals) and cf_agent_can_rout (an agent may rout only if 10 x (dead+wounded+routed) > men still ready, i.e. about 9% losses), all_enemies_routed and agent_run_away. cf_can_spawn_as_body_guard spawns companions as bodyguards in town and hall scenes, and init_death_cam follows the player after death.

features.name: Spawn-time equipment variety and item-quality steps, plus blacksmith item improvement
features.summary: When a soldier spawns, his gear is reshuffled from his troop's inventory: a random helmet, armour or weapon from the allowed set, with surplus weapons dropped. Items can carry better or worse quality modifiers. A town or estate smith can upgrade an item one quality step for a fee.
features.mechanics: ti_on_agent_spawn triggers in 25 templates (e.g. mst:bandit_lair/t43, 256 stmts) collect the troop's inventory items of a type with their modifiers (troop_get_inventory_slot_modifier), shuffle them (shuffle_troop_slots) and agent_equip_item one with its modifier. They also unequip duplicate one-handed or two-handed weapons and handle special troops. get_next_higher_imod_for_item / get_next_lower_imod_for_item (77/75 callers) step a modifier along the quality ladder, and get_item_modifier_effects names it. Smith dialogs (dlg:9564 item_improve, dlg:11325 lat_item_improve) quote and apply one step up. evaluate_item / equip_best_melee_weapon pick the best weapon for AI.
evidence: dis acan mst:bandit_lair/t43:conseq: inventory collection by item type with modifiers, shuffle, agent_equip_item with modifier, duplicate weapon removal

features.name: Siege planning (blockade, sanitation, traitors, infiltration, ambushes, starvation, fortified siege camp): inherited Brytenwalda/VC system
features.summary: Before assaulting, the besieger meets advisers to set up a blockade, look for a traitor inside, infiltrate, ambush relief forces and fortify the siege camp. Defenders starve and may sally, surrender or die. This is the same Brytenwalda-lineage siege system that VC and 457 AD carry.

features.name: Drivable chariots and chariot races (requires WSE2)
features.summary: Chariot 'horses' are items that spawn a chariot prop the rider drives, with crash and high-speed damage and a chariot camera. Dismounting a chariot needs a non-vanilla opcode, and the module itself says chariot races need WSE2.
features.mechanics: init_chariot_item (ti_on_init_item on itm_basic_chariot_horse / _b_horse / quadriga) sets up the prop. chariot_trigger (522 call sites, every 0.5 s) moves the prop with the horse agent and calls check_chariots_crashed. chariot_on_destruction handles breakage.
